@angelorodem I am unable to reproduce this in both 4.5-beta3 and latest `master`, so please provide an MRP.

> RigidBody3D set to “Sleeping” on start.

This hasn't worked in Godot (for either physics engine) in a very long time, if ever, as `RigidBody3D` will have its transform set immediately after it's created, which wakes the body up.

> Directly sweep/move this frozen box through the side of the sleeping stack using a script

You say "frozen" but you don't mention actually enabling the `freeze` property. Setting the `sleeping` property wouldn't "freeze" the body in the way you seem to want, since the moment you move it in any way it'll wake up.

> It's easier/faster to create this in Godot than downloading a MRP.

For future reference, please provide an MRP for anything but the most trivial repro (e.g. start the editor and click this one button). It's not just about saving the maintainer/tester from having to recreate the scene, but also to make sure we're actually looking at the same thing, which I'm guessing is not the case here.

Ok, i need to rename the issue, it seems that sweeping Area3D over sleeping bodies takes them out of sleeping state.

here is a MRP
[minimal_project.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21316742/minimal_project.zip)

when the bodies are sleeping press E and sweep the disabled box over, 
it has a Area3D inside, when sweeping it over the pile, it takes the whole pile out of sleeping state.

not sure if this is expected, but it seems wrong, i would expect bodies that apply forces to be able to take another body from sleeping, or this is needed to make Area3D work?

just by logic alone i don't think that an intersection test should change physics proprieties of a RigidBody

i haven't checked if using a Shape query also takes the objs from sleeping state, but i'll probably test this out.

That is indeed a bit of an odd discrepancy between the two engines, which I was not aware of.

I wouldn't expect a body to be woken up by an `Area3D` like this. I'll have to take a closer look as to why it's happening, but it could very well just be a quirk with how Jolt manages waking up of bodies.

i confirmed that using PhysicsShapeQuery does not take the bodies out of sleeping state,
this is the approach i took to mitigate the issue on my side, but i still think this should fixed

The reason why pressing E activates the pile is that it spawns a `NiceBox` at (0, 0, 0) which intersects with the pile. As the Area3D of the new box intersects with the pile it goes through this code path:

```
JPH::BodyManager::ActivateBodies(const JPH::BodyID * inBodyIDs, int inNumber) Line 551	C++
JPH::BodyInterface::ActivateBodyInternal(JPH::Body & ioBody) Line 25	C++
JPH::BodyInterface::ActivateBody(const JPH::BodyID & inBodyID) Line 219	C++
JoltSpace3D::set_is_object_sleeping(const JPH::BodyID & p_jolt_id, bool p_enable) Line 483	C++
JoltBody3D::set_is_sleeping(bool p_enabled) Line 688	C++
JoltBody3D::wake_up() Line 181	C++
JoltBody3D::_motion_changed() Line 476	C++
JoltBody3D::_update_damp() Line 363	C++
JoltBody3D::_areas_changed() Line 464	C++
JoltBody3D::add_area(JoltArea3D * p_area) Line 1037	C++
JoltArea3D::_notify_body_entered(const JPH::BodyID & p_body_id) Line 194	C++
JoltArea3D::body_shape_entered(const JPH::BodyID & p_body_id, const JPH::SubShapeID & p_other_shape_id, const JPH::SubShapeID & p_self_shape_id) Line 466	C++
JoltContactListener3D::_flush_area_enters() Line 505	C++
JoltContactListener3D::post_step() Line 567	C++
JoltSpace3D::_post_step(float p_step) Line 103	C++
JoltSpace3D::step(float p_step) Line 221	C++
JoltPhysicsServer3D::step(float p_step) Line 1633	C++
PhysicsServer3DWrapMT::step(float p_step) Line 64	C++
Main::iteration() Line 5015	C++
OS_Windows::run() Line 2354	C++
widechar_main(int argc, wchar_t * * argv) Line 98	C++
_main() Line 125	C++
```

Basically the `_areas_changed` message on the body triggers recalculation of the linear and angular damping values (because an `Area3D` can override it) and after doing that we unconditionally wake up the body. Note that that `_areas_changed` function also contains a call to `wake_up`, so it wakes it up twice.

Removing [these 2 calls](https://github.com/jrouwe/godot/tree/108715) fixes this bug. But there may be a reason why bodies entering an area need to be woken up... (e.g. if the gravity changes)

> But there may be a reason why bodies entering an area need to be woken up... (e.g. if the gravity changes)

Right, I forgot to actually report back here, but yes, that is indeed the reason (which I only realized once I stepped through the code as well).

I put in a number of `wake_up()` calls like that all over the place, where if something about the body's "environment" changed it would wake up so that it could react to those changes. I was always more worried about bodies remaining sleeping when they shouldn't be rather than the other way around, but I probably took it too far.

That `_motion_changed()` call in `_update_damp()` should rightfully only run if the total damping actually changed (if at all), but the way damping is updated in general has been broken for a while now, since (IIRC) it doesn't react to runtime changes of the area overrides. I've been meaning to move it to be done similar to how/when gravity is updated instead, as part of the space stepping, which is what Godot Physics does as well.

To also get rid of the one in `_areas_changed()` we'd presumably have to (redundantly) calculate the total gravity in `_areas_changed()` in order to see if the total gravity actually changed before we call `wake_up()`. It won't be perfect though, if two area changes happened that canceled eachother out, but that's a rare edge-case I guess.

I've now put up a (long overdue) fix for this: #118197

There might be more `wake_up()` calls that should get the same treatment though. I haven't looked too closely at them.
